pull.title: fuzz: Add a target that feeds arbitrary bytes to V2Transport
pull.body:
No fuzz target feeds V2Transport bytes that an honest peer would not send past the v2 key exchange. I add p2p_transport_v2_receive. It knows the keys of the transport it tests. It builds the input from arbitrary bytes and from the parts of a valid handshake: the peer key, garbage, the garbage terminator and encrypted packets, which may be corrupted. It feeds the input in pieces of arbitrary size. It reaches every v2 receive state and the failures on the way to them.

I ran it for about 13 minutes in total from an empty corpus, with libFuzzer and the address and undefined sanitizers, and it found no crash. Replaying the corpus gets both accepted and rejected messages out of the transport.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.

comments.body:
```suggestion
    const auto ent{ConsumeFixedLengthByteVector<std::byte>(provider, 32)};
    const auto peer_ent{ConsumeFixedLengthByteVector<std::byte>(provider, 32)};
```

nit: I think `ConsumeFixedLengthByteVector<std::byte>(provider, 32)` does the same consume-then-resize and lets these be `const`:
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/test/fuzz/util.h#L280

It should read the input the same way.

nit: the `BIP324Cipher(key, ent)` constructor calls `key.EllSwiftCreate(ent)` and nothing else:
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a773e1e33b349dc819b5a0edc1c7a4839dc73b48/src/bip324.cpp#L25-L29

Maybe call that instead of building a second cipher? It gives the same public key.


```suggestion
    peer.Initialize(key.EllSwiftCreate(ent), /*initiator=*/!initiating);
```

nit: `stream` and `aad` hold `uint8_t`, but most bytes going in are `std::byte`. That forces casts both ways: `UCharCast` in `append_fn`, and `MakeByteSpan` / `MakeWritableByteSpan` for `Encrypt`.

Maybe store `std::byte` and convert once with `MakeUCharSpan(stream)` before `ReceivedBytes()`? I think that also removes the duplicate insert in the "Arbitrary bytes" and "Garbage" branches, and it reads the input the same way.

nit: the code doesn't use `more` or `msg_type`.

```suggestion
        const auto& [bytes, _more, _msg_type] = transport.GetBytesToSend(/*have_next_message=*/false);
```
